question: Who is Natalia Vegman and what is her background?
answer: Natalia is a software engineer by education who spent 14 years at Murmansk Shipping Company — one of Russia's largest maritime transport enterprises — rising from engineer to Head of the entire IT & Telecommunications Service, managing a team of ~40 people. The team built a proprietary ERP, implemented SAP, 1C, and Company Media, and administered an on-premises data center. Seven years ago she relocated to Saint Petersburg and transitioned into AI consulting, applying the same systems-thinking discipline to production-ready intelligent systems. She now has 19 years of total IT experience and specializes in multimodal LLM architectures, enterprise DWH design, and end-to-end AI automation.

question: In which industries do you have deep domain expertise?
answer: My primary commercial sectors are: 1) Hospitality & Property Management — async FastAPI backends, Bnovo PMS API integration, RAG-powered guest helpdesks. 2) Maritime Logistics & Fisheries — scalable PostgreSQL DWH for quota management, parsing federal registries (Cerberus, FGIS Mercury), AMP vessel tracking. 3) Fishing Industry Competitor Monitoring — desktop crawlers, headless Selenium, GPT-4o structured analysis. 4) Fashion & Style Tech — Gemini Vision wardrobe analysis, Virtual Try-On with fal.ai. 5) Content & Social Media Automation — GigaChat-powered Tone-of-Voice post generation for VK. 6) Genealogy — GEDCOM-based family-tree platforms.

question: What is your core AI and data engineering tech stack?
answer: My production stack: Python (FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2.0, Alembic, pandas, Flask), PostgreSQL, ChromaDB, FAISS. AI/ML layer: OpenAI (GPT-4o/Vision), Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini 2.5 (Flash/Pro), Sber GigaChat, OpenRouter (multi-provider LLM routing with fallback), Hugging Face (Transformers, PEFT/LoRA, TRL SFTTrainer, BitsAndBytes 4-bit quantization), Yandex SpeechKit (STT/TTS), fal.ai (Virtual Try-On). Agent orchestration: Hermes, OpenClaw, MCP, n8n. Infra: Docker, nginx, systemd, certbot, GitHub Pages.

question: Do you build simple chatbots or complex backend systems?
answer: I engineer autonomous digital workers and comprehensive AI pipelines. My systems interact with production databases, extract business parameters from unstructured inputs (PDF documents, map layouts, image attachments, voice messages), compute complex real-time metrics (occupancy rates, ADR, quota balances, logistics trends), and push structured sync alerts to CRM (Bitrix24, AmoCRM) — all within secure, containerized Docker environments.

question: Can you design and build multi-agent AI systems?
answer: Yes. I design production-ready multi-agent systems where specialized AI agents operate under a central orchestrator. Each agent has a defined role (researcher, developer, designer), its own model, and its own cognitive context. The orchestrator receives a task, identifies the relevant business domain from a library of 7 domains, and delegates to appropriate subagents via a structured Shared State protocol — eliminating direct coupling between agents. Supports parallel task execution and horizontal scaling without rewiring the system.

question: Do you offer AI architecture consulting for businesses?
answer: Yes, this is one of my core service offerings. I audit existing business processes, identify where AI delivers measurable ROI, select the optimal technology stack (models, providers, infrastructure), and design the full system with explicit constraints around data security, budget, and scalability. The deliverable is not a generic recommendation deck — it is a concrete architectural blueprint with justified rationale for every technical decision and a phased implementation roadmap.

question: Do you have experience fine-tuning Large Language Models?
answer: Yes. I have practical R&D experience in Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT/LoRA) on open-source foundation models (ruGPT-3, Qwen architectures). I can engineer custom instruction datasets, configure LoRA adapters to modify an LLM's Tone of Voice to match brand guidelines, and prepare models for local offline deployment (Ollama/GGUF) to ensure absolute data privacy compliance.

question: How do you ensure data security in your AI systems?
answer: Security is built into the architecture from the start: Docker container isolation, Row-Level Security (RLS) on relational databases, webhook validation using secret API tokens (Telegram X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token), Feature Flags / Kill Switches to gracefully deactivate individual microservices during incidents, and HTTPS with Let's Encrypt on all public endpoints. For sensitive data, local LLM deployment (offline inference) is available as an option.

question: Tell me about the personal HR agent on this website.
answer: This very site is one of my projects. It's a bilingual (EN/RU) AI portfolio with a FastAPI RAG backend, FAISS vector search over my CV and FAQ documents, and a GPT-4o chat widget. The language is auto-detected from the visitor's browser and passed to the backend, which switches both the system prompt (HR agent persona) and the FAISS retrieval filter. The static frontend is hosted on GitHub Pages at vegman.dev, the API runs on a VPS behind nginx + Let's Encrypt. Source: github.com/natavegman/portfolio-site

question: What is the MyFamilyTree project?
answer: MyFamilyTree is a personal side project born from a genuine interest in genealogy and family history research. It's a FastAPI backend that imports GEDCOM family-tree files, parses person and family records into a PostgreSQL database via SQLAlchemy, and exposes REST endpoints for searching relatives and attaching archival documents (birth certificates, photos, emigration papers) to individual records. Docker Compose for local development. Source: github.com/natavegman/MyFamilyTree

question: What is your legal status and contract workflow for international clients?
answer: I operate under formal Service Agreements as a registered Sole Proprietor. I hold e-Resident status in Kazakhstan, enabling smooth legal contracting and multi-currency B2B invoicing with international clients. Project costs are scoped based on architectural blueprint complexity.
